ety.text: Inherited from stems with an intervocalic -m-, either primary one or secondarily originated from -p- or -v- (which develop via -ṽ- into -m-). The -m- is lost after having nasalized the following vowel. See -आ (-ā).

x: हिमालय के शिखरों से आने वाली अतिशीतल हवाओं ने घाटी में ठिठुरन बढ़ा दी है।

ety.text: Borrowed from Sanskrit अनुजा (anujā). By surface analysis, अनुज (anuj, “born after”) + -आ (-ā).

s.g: a female given name, Anuja, from Sanskrit

ety.text: Borrowed from Sanskrit अनुजा (anujā). By surface analysis, अनुज (anuj, “born after”) + -आ (-ā).

s.g: Āstīka, a rishi, son of Jaratkaru and Manasa, who saved the naga race from being destroyed in King Janamejaya's Sarpa Satra yajna
x: ऋषि आस्तीक ने राजा जनमेजय के सर्प सत्र यज्ञ को रोककर सर्पों की रक्षा की।

s.g: bangle, bracelet, usually made of metal

ety.text: Borrowed from Punjabi ਕੰਗਣ (kaṅgaṇ), ਕੰਗਨ (kaṅgan), from Prakrit 𑀓𑀁𑀓𑀡 (kaṃkaṇa), from Sanskrit कङ्कण (kaṅkaṇa). Doublet of ककना (kaknā).

s.g: Kabul (a river in Afghanistan and Pakistan)

ety.text: Borrowed from Sanskrit गाम्भीर्य (gāmbhīrya), from गम्भीर (gambhīra).

x: इस चुनाव में जीतने की संभावना है।

s.g: land liable to be flooded or inundated land

ety.text: Perhaps from Punjabi, related to डूबना (ḍūbnā). Don't confuse with दुबसी (dubsī).

x: वह तरह-तरह की बातें करता है।

s.g: to break apart, separate; cause to break
weight of 5 kg; or the quantity corresponding it

x: दारा इतने लंबे सफ़र के बाद अलेक्ज़ेंडर की फ़ौज थककर चूर हो गई होगी। हम आज रात ही उन पर हमला करके उन्हें चकनाचूर कर देंगे। […] अक्स्यार्टस मगर इसके लिए हमारी फ़ौज नाकाफ़ी है। […] हमारी छोटी सी फ़ौज को अलेक्ज़ेंडर मसलके रख देगा।

ety.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian نَاکَافِی (nākāfī). By surface analysis, ना- (nā-) + काफ़ी (kāfī).

s.g: Nishakara, a rishi in the Ramayana

x: कतनी क़दीम कितना नईम, सब दुनिया से न्यारा

ety.text: Inherited from Sanskrit *अन्याकार (*anyākāra, “different”), from अन्य (anyá, “other”) + आकार (ākāra, “form, shape”). Cognate with Punjabi ਨਿਆਰਾ (niārā), Gujarati ન્યારું (nyārũ), Marathi न्यारा (nyārā), Odia ନିଆରା (niārā).

x: संयुक्त राष्ट्र आर्थिक एवं सामाजिक परिषद

ety.text: Renaming of अजोधन (ajodhan) to पाक (pāk) + पत्तन (pattan).

Inherited from Prakrit 𑀧𑁄𑀢𑁆𑀣𑀬 (pŏtthaya, “book”) or 𑀧𑀼𑀢𑁆𑀣𑀬 (putthaya), from Sanskrit पवस्त (pavasta, “covering”) and Sanskrit पुस्तक (pustaka, “book”). The latter is a borrowing from some Middle Iranian language (see there). Both are ultimately from Proto-Indo-Iranian *pawástam (“covering, envelope”). Doublet of पुस्तक (pustak) and पोस्त (post).

s.g: a surname, equivalent to English Bansal
Buddhist, of or pertaining to Buddhism

ety.text: Borrowed from Sanskrit बौद्ध (bauddha), vṛddhi derivative of बुद्ध (buddha).
Inherited from Sanskrit मृष्ट (mṛṣṭa, “rubbed, washed, pure”), from the root मृज् (mṛj, “to wipe, cleanse”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₃merǵ-
Borrowed from Arabic يَسُوع (yasūʕ), from Aramaic ישוע (yešú‘), from Hebrew ישוע (yešûa‘), a contracted form of יהושע (yəhôšua‘, “Joshua”). Doublet of यीशु (yīśu) and यसू (yasū).

s.g: a very fine type of muslin

ety.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian شَبْنَم (šabnam). By surface analysis, शब (śab, “night”) + नम (nam, “moisture”). Compare Bengali শবনম (śobnom), Punjabi ਸ਼ਬਨਮ (śabnam).

s.g: a female given name, Shabnam, from Persian

ety.text: Borrowed from Classical Persian شَبْنَم (šabnam). By surface analysis, शब (śab, “night”) + नम (nam, “moisture”). Compare Bengali শবনম (śobnom), Punjabi ਸ਼ਬਨਮ (śabnam).

s.g: abbreviation of संयुक्त राज्य (sãyukt rājya, “United States”)
abbreviation of संयुक्त राष्ट्र (sãyukt rāṣṭra, “United Nations”)

ety.text: सुध (sudh) + -ना (-nā), from Sanskrit शुद्ध (śuddha). Doublet of सुध (sudh), सूधा (sūdhā), and शुद्ध (śuddh).

s.g: Hathras (a city and district of Aligarh division, Uttar Pradesh, India)
